LESSON: INTERACTIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.3: Interactive Speaking
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Interactive Speaking, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 8 MANDARIN.

Key inquiry question: what happens in the essential places provided in the given pictures with peers, ● practise using “要去” and “做什么?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. restate key words and phrases in varied listening contexts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Interactive Speaking in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply non-verbal cues appropriately to enhance communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Interactive Speaking in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. exhibit interest in speaking clearly while interacting with others.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Interactive Speaking in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. restate key words and phrases in varied listening contexts,

   Interactive Speaking helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. apply non-verbal cues appropriately to enhance communication,

   Interactive Speaking helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. exhibit interest in speaking clearly while interacting with others.

   Interactive Speaking helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to an audio clip on essential places in town (车站、派出所、学 校、邮局、医院、银行、商场) and repeat the words,
2. search online for an audio-visual narration of a town, and point out the places identified collaboratively,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Interactive Speaking together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy: the learner develops skills in connecting to digital technology as they carry out a simple online search for audio- visual materials related to essential places in the town.

Values:
Responsibility: the learner collaboratively engages in assigned roles and duties as they take turns to construct simple sentences

with peers.

(PCIs):

they simulate the skit with peers.

Link to Other Learning Areas:
